cards.title: Client
cards.body: Healthcare company providing online CPR certification, healthcare CPR training, and CPR card services

cards.title: Service Delivered
cards.body: Targeted link building through guest posts and niche-relevant placements on healthcare, medical education, and professional certification publications

cards.title: Primary Goal
cards.body: Grow organic traffic significantly beyond the existing 35,000 monthly visitors and capture high-intent search traffic for healthcare certification and CPR training keywords

sections.title: Competing in a High-Trust Healthcare Niche
sections.lead: The healthcare certification and CPR training space is one of the most trust-sensitive niches in organic search. Google applies heightened scrutiny to health-related content and websites, making domain authority, editorial credibility, and strong E-E-A-T signals important factors in achieving and maintaining rankings.

blocks.x: At the start of the campaign, the client had a meaningful organic presence with approximately 35,000 monthly organic traffic. However, more established certification providers and healthcare training platforms continued to dominate the top three positions on high-value queries like "CPR certification," "HIPAA certification," and "BLS recertification."
With an 11-month campaign window, every link needed to support pages with the strongest ranking and commercial potential.

cards.title: High-Trust Niche Requires Editorial Credibility
cards.body: Google applies E-E-A-T scrutiny to healthcare content. Links from credible healthcare and medical publishers play an important role in supporting visibility.

cards.title: Established Certification Providers in Top Positions
cards.body: National health organizations and large certification bodies already held strong positions with authority built over many years.

cards.title: Certification Pages Needed Targeted Link Equity
cards.body: The highest-value pages — CPR certification, healthcare CPR card, and recertification pages — needed stronger external authority signals to move on their primary keywords.

sections.title: The Strategy: Precision Authority in a High-Stakes Niche
sections.lead: Healthcare SEO demands a more disciplined approach to link building. Every element of this campaign was designed around editorial credibility, topical relevance, and E-E-A-T standards.

cards.title: Certification Page Priority Targeting
cards.body: The campaign prioritized certification and training pages based on commercial value and ranking potential. CPR certification, healthcare CPR card, and recertification pages received links first, focusing authority on the pages most closely tied to traffic and conversions.

cards.title: Healthcare and Medical Publisher Network
cards.body: Every link was placed on publishers with genuine credibility in the healthcare, medical education, and clinical training space. The campaign focused on health and wellness websites, medical publications, and healthcare training resources with strong topical alignment.

cards.title: E-E-A-T-Aligned Anchor Strategy
cards.body: We built a carefully balanced mix of partial-match anchors targeting specific certification queries, branded anchors reinforcing domain identity, and natural descriptive anchors to maintain a penalty-safe profile. Anchor distribution was adjusted throughout based on ranking movement.

cards.title: Guest Posts and Contextual Placements
cards.body: The strategy combined contextual placements in established healthcare content with guest posts on medical education and healthcare publications, balancing stronger contextual relevance with greater control over content and anchor placement.

sections.title: How Tanot Solutions Executed the Campaign
sections.lead: The campaign followed a phased approach across 11 months, focused on establishing E-E-A-T credibility through to reaching the 48K+ visitor milestone.

cards.title: E-E-A-T Foundation Phase
cards.body: The first three months focused on establishing editorial credibility signals. Links were placed on credible healthcare and medical education publishers, primarily targeting certification pages with natural, branded anchors to establish stronger trust and topical relevance.

cards.title: Certification Keyword Targeting Phase
cards.body: As E-E-A-T signals strengthened, we introduced partial-match anchors targeting "CPR certification," "healthcare CPR card," and related certification queries. Organic traffic trends began showing stronger upward movement as visibility improved on priority pages.

cards.title: Traffic Acceleration Phase
cards.body: The compound effect of consistent, topically credible link building accelerated significantly. Traffic continued increasing month over month. The campaign expanded beyond certification pages to include CPR resources and recertification guides, broadening overall keyword visibility.

cards.title: Consolidation Phase: 48K+ Visitors Confirmed
cards.body: The final two months focused on protecting rankings gained and pushing borderline top-3 positions over the line. By month 11, the campaign confirmed 48,000+ monthly organic visitors, with 11,600 total keywords ranked and 1,700 in the top 3.

sections.title: Key Metrics Over 11 Months
sections.lead: The campaign ran across 11 months, focusing on strengthening authority, expanding keyword visibility, and increasing organic traffic.

blocks.alt: 35K to 48K+ monthly visitors in 11 months: healthcare company

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.lead: Questions we hear most from healthcare providers, certification companies, and medical education businesses considering link building in a YMYL niche.

items.q: Is link building safe for a healthcare website? Does Google penalize it?
items.a: White-hat link building is not only safe for healthcare websites but also necessary. Google expects healthcare sites to earn editorial links from credible health and medical publishers as part of stronger E-E-A-T signals. Every link in this campaign came from real publishers with genuine organic traffic, and the campaign ran for 11 months with zero penalties.

items.q: Why does publisher credibility matter so much in healthcare SEO?
items.a: Google applies YMYL (Your Money Your Life) standards to healthcare content. A link from a respected medical education site or health and wellness publication carries significantly more value than a high-DR link from an unrelated industry. In healthcare, topical and editorial credibility are the primary drivers of ranking authority.

items.q: How did traffic grow from 35K to 48K so consistently?
items.a: The consistent growth curve reflects the compounding effect of month-over-month link acquisition. Each month's link equity built on the authority gained from the previous month's placements, becoming more visible from months 4 to 6 when keyword rankings began accelerating.

items.q: Are the links permanent? Will traffic drop if we stop building?
items.a: Editorial backlinks are permanent placements. The referring domains built during the campaign continue passing authority over time. Traffic does not immediately decline if link building pauses; however, continuing to build relevant links can help maintain momentum as other sites continue investing in SEO.

items.q: Can link building help a healthcare brand appear in AI results?
items.a: Increasingly, yes. Editorial credibility built through healthcare publisher placements can support discoverability not only in traditional search results but also across AI-assisted search experiences including ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and AI Overviews.

cards.title: High-Impact Page Targeting
cards.body: Links were directed to pages with the highest commercial value, including the core platform page, inventory management features, and analytics landing pages rather than distributing links across the site.

cards.title: Topically Relevant Publisher Selection
cards.body: All links were placed on publishers aligned with Amazon sellers, e-commerce, and SaaS audiences. Relevance was prioritized over general authority to improve ranking stability in a niche market.

cards.title: Keyword-Intentional Anchor Strategy
cards.body: A structured anchor mix was used to balance keyword relevance and natural distribution. Anchors were selected to support rankings without over-optimization, combining branded, descriptive, and partial-match terms.

cards.title: Contextual Placements and Guest Posts
cards.body: The campaign combined contextual placements in existing articles with guest posts for greater control over placement and anchors. The mix was adjusted based on performance during the campaign.

sections.title: How Tanot Solutions Executed the Campaign
sections.lead: The campaign was executed over four months, with each phase building on early authority gains and focusing on pages with the highest impact potential.

cards.title: Audit and Foundation: Identifying the Fastest Wins
cards.body: We began with a full competitive link gap analysis to identify which pages competitors were earning links to. Initial links went to the core platform page, using branded and partial-match anchors to establish early authority signals.

cards.title: Commercial Page Push: Sending Equity Where It Counts
cards.body: With the core page receiving initial authority, link acquisition shifted to high-intent feature and product pages. Links to the inventory management page, the pricing analytics tool, and the listing optimizer page began moving long-tail ranking clusters that had been completely stagnant.

cards.title: Scaling and Consolidation: Doubling Down on What Moved
cards.body: Month 3 tracking showed clear ranking movement on key terms. Link efforts were doubled to the best-performing pages and added supporting links to blog content nearing page 1. By the end of month 4, organic traffic had increased from 1,000 to 2,000+ monthly visitors, with continued upward momentum.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.lead: Questions we hear most from SaaS founders and e-commerce businesses considering link building with a short or defined timeline.

items.q: Can link building really double traffic in just 4 months?
items.a: Yes, when the strategy is focused on high-impact pages from the start. In this campaign, ranking improvements began within the first few months, contributing to measurable traffic growth by month 4.

items.q: How do you choose which pages to target with links?
items.a: We start with a competitive link gap analysis to identify which pages your top-ranking competitors are getting linked to that you are not. We then overlay commercial intent, so the pages closest to a sale or trial get links first.

items.q: Is 35 links enough to make a real difference?
items.a: In many cases, yes. When links are placed on relevant, credible publishers and directed to the right pages, a smaller number of high-quality placements can drive meaningful results.

items.q: Will the results hold after the campaign ends?
items.a: Editorial backlinks remain live and continue to pass authority over time. As a result, rankings and traffic may continue to improve beyond the initial campaign period.

items.q: Are the links safe? No risk of penalties?
items.a: We focus on editorial, contextually relevant placements and avoid manipulative tactics such as PBNs, link farms, or automated schemes. All publishers are reviewed before outreach. This campaign ran four months with zero manual actions or algorithmic issues.

items.q: Can link building help with AI search visibility for SaaS tools?
items.a: Strong editorial signals can contribute to visibility across AI-driven search platforms. In this campaign, the domain began appearing in responses across tools such as ChatGPT, reflecting increased authority beyond traditional search.

sections.title: Project Overview
sections.lead: A resume builder SaaS with strong product-market fit engaged Tanot Solutions to scale its organic growth beyond 1 million monthly visitors. The goal was to build sustained link authority to compete with category leaders and expand visibility across high-value keywords.

blocks.x: Every day without domain authority was a day the competition widened the gap. The cost of inaction compounds just like the cost of a great link campaign but in reverse. Tanot Solutions understood this and delivered a campaign that moved both our rankings and our traffic consistently over 18 months.
blocks.name: Resume Builder SaaS

cards.title: Client
cards.body: Resume Builder SaaS offering AI-assisted templates, cover letter tools, and career resources for job seekers

cards.title: Service Delivered
cards.body: End-to-end link building including guest posts, contextual insertions, structured anchor strategy, and phased page prioritization

cards.title: Primary Goal
cards.body: Increase organic traffic beyond 1 million monthly visitors and strengthen domain authority in the career tech space

sections.title: Competing in a Highly Competitive Search Landscape
sections.lead: The resume builder and career tools category is one of the most link-competitive niches in SaaS. Top-ranking platforms have DR 70+ profiles, thousands of referring domains, and content libraries built over years making it difficult to gain or sustain top rankings.

blocks.x: At 1 million monthly visitors, the client had already achieved strong traction. However, closing the gap with category leaders required more than increasing link volume it required a structured approach to building high-quality, contextually relevant links to the right pages over time.
Without consistent, targeted link acquisition, growth risked plateauing as competitors continued to strengthen their authority.

cards.title: Strong Competitor Authority
cards.body: Top competitors had DR 75+ profiles with large, established backlink portfolios. Maintaining the gap required sustained, consistent link acquisition.

cards.title: Highly Competitive Keywords
cards.body: High-value keywords such as "resume templates" and "AI cover letter generator" required sustained, topically relevant editorial links to improve and maintain rankings.

cards.title: Commercial Pages Needed Deeper Link Equity
cards.body: Template collections, the core builder tool, and career advice pages needed targeted link equity to widen the keyword footprint and deepen rankings.

sections.title: Strategy Built for Sustained Authority Growth
sections.lead: We implemented a structured link acquisition strategy across four core areas: page prioritization, publisher selection, anchor optimization, and link type diversification executed consistently over 18 months.

cards.title: Target Page Prioritization
cards.body: Links were allocated based on commercial value and ranking potential, with a focus on high-impact pages such as the resume builder tool, template collections, and career content not just the homepage.

cards.title: Topically Relevant Publisher Selection
cards.body: All links were placed on publishers with strong topical alignment to career development, HR, and job search. Relevance was prioritized over raw authority to support long-term ranking stability.

cards.title: Anchor Text Optimization
cards.body: A structured anchor strategy was used to maintain semantic relevance while avoiding over-optimization. Anchor distribution was reviewed and adjusted regularly based on performance data.

cards.title: Guest Posts and Niche Edits Combined
cards.body: We combined guest posts (for editorial control) with contextual placements in existing articles (for faster authority transfer). The mix was adjusted throughout the campaign based on observed results.

sections.title: How Tanot Solutions Executed the Campaign Strategy
sections.lead: The campaign was executed in four phases over 18 months, with each stage building on the authority gained in the previous phase.

cards.title: Foundation Phase: Strengthening Key Pages
cards.body: The initial phase focused on identifying which commercial pages had ranking proximity to the top 5 and needed additional link equity to break through. High-DR links were placed on core product pages and the template collection. Early ranking improvements on mid-competition terms were visible by the end of month 4.

cards.title: Keyword Targeting Phase: Focused Authority on High-Intent Pages
cards.body: With authority signals strengthening, the focus shifted to deep-linking high-intent commercial pages. Placements on relevant HR and career publications drove topical relevance signals, helping key pages move from page 2 to page 1.

cards.title: Scaling Phase: Widening the Keyword Coverage
cards.body: Link acquisition expanded to secondary pages, including the cover letter builder, career advice blog clusters, and specific template pages, widening the overall keyword footprint. New referring domains were added consistently, bringing total referring domains to over 8,300 by this phase.

cards.title: Consolidation Phase: Sustaining Growth and Authority
cards.body: The final phase focused on maintaining rankings and strengthening domain authority. By month 18, monthly organic traffic had grown to 1.7 million monthly visitors a 70% increase from the 1 million baseline. The domain had accumulated 99.5K total backlinks and established itself as a recognized authority in the career tech space, attracting additional links organically.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.lead: Questions we hear most often from SaaS founders and marketing leaders considering a link building engagement with Tanot Solutions.

items.q: How long before we see results from link building?
items.a: Initial ranking movement often appears within 60 to 90 days, particularly for lower-competition keywords. More meaningful traffic growth typically occurs between months 4 and 6 as authority builds. For a domain already at a significant scale like this one, results continue to compound over time.

items.q: Is this white-hat? Will my site get penalized?
items.a: Every link is white-hat, editorial, and Google-compliant. We do not use PBNs, link farms, or automated schemes. All publishers are vetted manually before any outreach begins. This campaign ran 18 months with zero manual actions or algorithmic penalties.

items.q: What industries do you work with?
items.a: We primarily work with SaaS, B2B services, and e-commerce companies operating in competitive niches. This includes sectors such as career tech, HR software, fintech, legal tech, and marketing platforms. The link building principles are universal what changes is the publisher network and anchor strategy for each niche.

items.q: How many links do we need per month?
items.a: Link volume depends on your current authority, competitive landscape, and target keywords. In this campaign, we built an average of 12 to 15 high-quality links per month, prioritizing relevance and impact over volume. We give a custom recommendation during your free strategy session based on a competitive analysis of your specific situation.

items.q: Do you provide reporting and transparency?
items.a: Yes, completely. Every client receives a monthly link report detailing every placement: publisher URL, live link URL, domain rating, estimated traffic, and anchor text used. Alongside the link report, a monthly performance update covers ranking movements and traffic trends. There are no black boxes.

items.q: Can link building improve visibility in AI search platforms?
items.a: Yes. This campaign shows that strong editorial link signals can contribute to visibility across AI platforms. The domain earned citations across tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini, reflecting increased authority beyond traditional search. A strong link profile built for Google rankings simultaneously builds AI recommendation visibility.
